en.focus: The rulebook makes the game playable
topics: Rules are part of the game
en.caption: Why the document in the box is part of the game experience itself.
See how one person can need different kinds of help at different moments.

en.focus: Make learning spread across the table
topics: Measure if a player can teach
en.caption: The central test is whether a reader can learn, teach and use the rules.

en.focus: Build a path through the rules
en.caption: Anatomy and order give readers the vocabulary they need before detailed play.
Pick a structure for both learning the game and finding a rule later.

en.focus: Write sentences players can act on
en.caption: A rule sentence should lead different readers to the same action.
Consistent terms make rules easier to learn, search and translate.

en.focus: Show the case people will argue about
en.caption: Useful examples reveal interactions that plain text leaves open to debate.
A reference system turns a long book into an answer people can reach quickly.
Typography and page structure determine whether rules remain usable in play.

en.focus: Put repeat rules where players look
en.caption: Player aids support the rulebook with quick guidance at the table.

en.focus: Make the rules work for more people
en.caption: Accessible and translatable rules start with design and writing choices.
The rulebook changes through testing, editing and production checks.
Blind testing shows what happens when the writer cannot explain the rules.

en.focus: Name the failure before fixing it
en.caption: Different failure modes call for different repairs.

en.focus: Study what happened in real games
en.caption: Case studies make abstract advice concrete and testable.
Reusable templates help you apply the handbook to your own game.
